title: Independent Imag8-only rejection hypothesis for i8-to-i1 truncation (0023)
summary: The independent claim that an Imag8 source rejects the s8-to-s1 pattern is disproved at vendor pin 8be0546 and saved upstream 742d554: both classes map to Any, and the generated matcher inserts an Ac copy. All 72 compiler runs and 48 selection checks pass. No fix or red baseline is claimed; the unrecovered historical #320 far-pointer observation remains qualified.

scope: Only the proposed independent Imag8 register-class rejection cause. This disposition does not invalidate the separate original #320 far-pointer observation or the native s32-to-s16 portion of patch 0023.
invalidation_reason: The report confuses a register-bank predicate with a register-class intersection test. The retained matcher has only s1/s8 type and Any-bank predicates for this rule, with no CPU or producer condition. MOS maps Imag8, Ac, and one-bit classes to Any. Class incompatibility creates a new Ac register and COPY during instruction constraint rather than rejecting the match. Thus a valid banked Imag8(s8)-to-s1 G_TRUNC cannot fail because its source is Imag8. Source-contract evidence at both recorded revisions establishes the reporting error independently of the passing probes.

status_history.reason: Independent Imag8-only rejection cause disproved by matcher and register-bank contract; historical far-pointer scope preserved.
